text:
Connor McMichael's first season in St. Louis has been a story of bad bounces. He has 3 goals and 11 points in 22 games after the move from Washington, and our numbers say the Blues have scored about nine fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice. That's the biggest "due" gap on the team, and it usually swings back.

The goal he did get on Nov. 18 against Anaheim was a beauty, batted out of mid-air past Ville Husso. Days earlier Yahoo Sports framed his shootout winner as something that masked the Blues' deeper scoring trouble, and that's fair: the whole group around him has gone cold.

Not all of it is luck. St. Louis gets about 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five, nearly three points worse than without him, and Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season with opponents generating more against him than almost any forward. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows where his game lives: 60% of his shots come off the rush. Watch his transition chances. If they keep coming, so will the points.
